newsitem.title: INDIA: Left-wing militants kill 16 Indian police.
newsitem.headline: Left-wing militants kill 16 Indian police.

text.p: Left-wing extremists attacked a remote police station in southern India on Friday, killing at least 16 people, authorities said.
Some 60 members of the outlawed People's War Group (PWG) surrounded Karakagudem village in Andhra Pradesh state at around 1:30 a.m. (2000 GMT Thursday), police in the state capital Hyderabad said.
Two groups of guerrillas raided the police station, and militants and police exchanged gunfire for more than half an hour, they said.
The insurgents then attacked the police station with bombs, killing all 16 police inside. United News of India said two civilians were also killed.
The extremists escaped with 32 guns, police said.

The attack took place in Khammam district, about 170 km (105 miles) west of Hyderabad, near the central state of Madhya Pradesh. It was reported to police in a nearby town by crew members of a state-owned bus.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups who split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July of last year.
Andhra Pradesh had a year-long respite from major PWG attacks after former Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao granted a temporary amnesty in June 1995.

Police said Naxalites, who reject the Indian government and want to set up Maoist state of their own, were behind nearly 800 violent incidents in Andhra Pradesh last year, killing 156 people, including 42 police.
Friday's attack was the third by Naxalites on policemen since Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu outlawed the group in July.
In November, guerrillas from the same left-wing group killed 13 policemen and one civilian in a raid on a village police station in Andhra Pradesh.
On October 7, seven policemen were killed in the state's Warangal district when the PWG triggered a landmine as police passed while patrolling by-elections.
The PWG operates throughout the vast Dandakaranya region straddling the states of Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa.
Other Naxalites also operate in the sprawling eastern states of West Bengal and Bihar and the populous northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
